topbar.ownEdgeOfflineTip: Your self-hosted node is offline; tunnel traffic is temporarily routed through the platform. It will switch back automatically once your node is up.

orgSwitch.body1: After switching, this client re-handshakes with the edge node and takes over the tunnels of "{{name}}".
orgSwitch.body2: The tunnels of the current organization "{{name}}" will go offline temporarily (they recover automatically when you switch back).

region.reconnectBody: Retry connecting to the edge nodes in this region.
region.switchBody1: After switching, this client reconnects to the edge nodes in region "{{region}}".
region.switchBody2: Tunnels in the original region (their public addresses are pinned to that region) will no longer be reachable through this client; you'll need to recreate them in the new region (the public address will change). Node switching within the same region is automatic and unaffected.
region.parkedNote: The edge nodes in the current region are unreachable; reconnection has stopped. You can switch region manually from the top-right.

affinity.toOwnBody: This client will reconnect to your self-hosted node; tunnel data egresses from your own server (bandwidth/traffic is yours).
affinity.toPlatformBody: This client will reconnect to a platform edge node; tunnel data egresses from the platform (rate-limited/metered per your plan).
affinity.bodyNote: Switching reconnects the edge node; the tunnel's public address (pinned to a specific node) will change, so existing tunnels must be recreated.

overview.readOnlyDesc: Overdue billing or an exceeded quota puts the account in read-only mode, where new tunnels can't be created. Open the console for details.
overview.quotaExceededDesc: Once exceeded, all existing tunnels keep working but no new ones can be added. Upgrade your plan or wait for next month's reset.
overview.selfHostedNotBilled: Self-hosted node · not counted toward plan
overview.edgeSelfTip: This tunnel currently routes through your org's self-hosted edge node (where switching the data node to "self-hosted" moves it).
overview.relaySelfTip: Currently homed on your org's self-hosted relay (where switching the data node to "self-hosted" moves it).
overview.notifReconnectingBody: The session with the edge node dropped; reconnecting automatically.
overview.notifFatalBody: Check the Logs page to find the cause.
overview.notifQuota100Body: Upgrade your plan, or wait for the next calendar month to reset.

tunnels.offlineNotConnectedTip: This client isn't connected to an edge node; the tunnel is temporarily offline.
tunnels.edgeDownTip: The edge node #{{id}} hosting this tunnel is offline; the tunnel is temporarily unavailable.
tunnels.onlineTip: Online — tunnel is live and serving.
tunnels.probeOkTip: Local probe OK ({{ms}}ms, {{n}} in a row)
tunnels.probeFailTip: Local probe failed: {{err}} ({{n}} in a row)
tunnels.serverOnlineTip: Online — served by another session of this client (e.g. a foreground 'calabi http'), or syncing
tunnels.heldByOtherClientTip: This tunnel is bound to another client in your org and isn't running on this machine.
tunnels.onlineOtherClientTip: Online — served by another client in your org, not this machine.

takeover.tip: Bring this tunnel to this machine
takeover.warnLocal: This machine will forward to the local address below — make sure that service is actually running here.
takeover.warnOther: The other client will stop serving this tunnel.
takeover.warnGap: The public URL stays the same, but expect a brief interruption while it moves here.
takeover.localTip: The local service on THIS machine to forward to (often differs from the original machine).
takeover.crossEdgeTip: This tunnel runs in another region/edge. Its public address is bound to that edge — an http/https subdomain is pinned there and a tcp/udp port is allocated there — so taking it over to this client would change (or break) the public address. Switch this client to the tunnel's region first, or recreate the tunnel here.

ipPolicy.title: IP access control
ipPolicy.hint: Allow or deny visitors by source IP / CIDR (one per line). Enforced at the edge.
ipPolicy.allow: Allowlist — only these may connect (leave empty to allow all)
ipPolicy.deny: Denylist — always blocked (wins over the allowlist)
ipPolicy.applyNote: Applied at the edge on save — no reconnect needed.

basicAuth.title: Basic authentication
basicAuth.hint: Require a username + password before visitors reach your service (HTTP/HTTPS tunnels). Passwords are hashed.

rateLimit.title: Rate limit
rateLimit.hint: Cap the rate of new connections to this tunnel (protects your upstream from floods). 0 / empty = unlimited.

headers.title: Request headers
headers.hint: Rewrite headers sent to your upstream (HTTP/HTTPS). Framing headers (Content-Length, etc.) can't be changed.
headers.name: Header

oauth.title: OAuth login wall
oauth.hint: Require visitors to sign in with an identity provider before reaching your service (HTTP/HTTPS).
oauth.callbackHint: Register this redirect/callback URL in your OAuth app:
oauth.allowEmails: Allowed emails (one per line; empty = any signed-in user)

security.title: Access control
security.lockedNotice: Some features require a plan upgrade to use: {{features}}.

edit.title: Edit tunnel
edit.endpointFixed: Type and public address can't be changed — create a new tunnel to use a different one.
edit.offMachineTitle: This tunnel runs on another machine
edit.offMachineDesc: Editing the name and security policy applies remotely. But “local address” points at the upstream on the machine that actually serves this tunnel — not this one. To run it here instead, use Takeover.
edit.offMachineLocalHint: This address applies to the other machine serving this tunnel.

tunnels.deleteConfirmDesc: It's removed from the edge node immediately; if a client is running, related connections are cut.
tunnels.cappedTooltip: Plan limit reached {{count}}/{{max}}; upgrade or delete existing tunnels and try again.
tunnels.cappedAlertDesc: Upgrade your plan or delete existing tunnels for the "New tunnel" button to become available again.
tunnels.edgeSwitchMsg: Switched cross-region to new edge node #{{current}} (the region of node #{{previous}} is unavailable)
tunnels.edgeSwitchDesc1: This client is now connected to an edge node in
tunnels.edgeSwitchDesc2: . Tunnel domains created in the previous region are temporarily unreachable — the region-wide wildcard is pinned to the original region and cross-region nodes don't forward to each other. Wait for the original region to recover and reconnect, or
tunnels.edgeSwitchDeleteRebuild: delete the tunnel and recreate it in the current region
tunnels.edgeSwitchDesc3: (the public address will change). Node switching within the same region is transparent and doesn't affect tunnel access.
tunnels.emptyText: No tunnels yet · click "New tunnel" in the top-right
tunnels.regionFilteredDesc: These tunnels are pinned to edges in other regions and can't be served from here. Switch region above, or see every region at once in the web console.
tunnels.mismatchTip: The client is connected to edge #{{clientEdge}}, but this tunnel's domain is pinned to edge #{{boundEdge}}, so the public address is unreachable. Switch the client back to edge #{{boundEdge}}, or delete and recreate the tunnel on the current edge (the public domain will change).
tunnels.pendingTip: Recorded on the server but not yet claimed by an edge. It syncs automatically once you start and sign in to the calabi client.

wizard.publishBannerDesc: The local address is filled from the service; pick a public type and address below. This is a separate public tunnel — it doesn't change the service's mesh access.
wizard.localAddrTip: The client forwards to this address, e.g. 127.0.0.1:8080
wizard.localAddrPublic: Use a local/intranet address (e.g. 127.0.0.1:8080 or a 10./192.168. host) — forwarding to a public address is not allowed.
wizard.localAddrFormat: Enter host:port (e.g. 127.0.0.1:8080 or localhost:3000) or a bare port.
wizard.remotePortTip: Leave blank to let the server assign one
wizard.customDomainRequired: Self-hosted egress requires your own domain
wizard.customDomainTip: Current egress is your self-hosted node: the public address uses your own domain. Point it to your self-hosted node's public IP, then complete verification / certificate binding in the web console under "Domains".
wizard.subdomainTip: Prefix only (e.g. myapp); the full address = prefix + the platform region subdomain (auto-generated, not editable). Leave blank for a random one. Custom domains are only available on self-hosted egress.
wizard.subdomainPattern: Lowercase letters / digits / hyphens only, and may not start or end with a hyphen
wizard.subdomainFreePlaceholder: Free plan assigns a random subdomain (choose your own after upgrading)
wizard.countHint: This organization already has {{team}} tunnels; a new one is appended to the list
wizard.countHintShared: This organization already has {{team}} tunnels ({{mine}} on this client); a new one is appended to the list
wizard.domainNoCertHint: This domain has no certificate yet: HTTP works now; HTTPS starts working once you issue a certificate under “Domains” in the web console.
wizard.localServiceTip: How the client dials your local service: HTTP connects in the clear, HTTPS wraps the connection in TLS (self-signed certificates are accepted).
wizard.checkFailHint: You can still create the tunnel — start the service and it will connect.
wizard.prefixCertNote: The HTTPS certificate is issued right after the tunnel is created — it takes a minute or two. HTTP works immediately.

reason.refused: Nothing is listening on that address yet.
reason.timeout: The address accepted nothing in time — it may be blocked by a firewall.
reason.unreachable: That address can't be reached from this machine.
reason.dns: That hostname doesn't resolve on this machine.
reason.tls: TLS failed. If your local service speaks plain HTTP, pick HTTP instead of HTTPS.
reason.http_5xx: The service answered, but with a server error.
reason.invalid: That address isn't a local one — a tunnel can only point at this machine or your own network.

wizard.preflightBody: You can create the tunnel anyway — it will connect as soon as the service is up.
wizard.prefixTipNode: Type a prefix only — the full address is <prefix>.{{suffix}}. Point *.{{suffix}} at {{ip}}, the node this client is connected to.
wizard.parentEmptyHint: This node serves no verified domain yet. Set its base_domain in the web console, and verify that domain under “Domains”.
wizard.apexInUse: {{name}} itself is already taken by the tunnel “{{tunnel}}”. Type a prefix.

inspector.title: Request inspector · {{name}}
inspector.noHttpHint: Only http / https tunnels are captured, and at least one visit is required.
inspector.replayTip: Resend this request to the local upstream

authGate.hint: If it stays unresponsive, check whether the daemon is running (tray → restart daemon)
authGate.serverUnreachableHint: The local daemon is running, but it can't reach the Calabi server (control plane). Check that the server is up and your network is connected.
authGate.daemonStarting: The local daemon is starting up...
authGate.daemonStartingHint: It's still initializing its connection — this usually clears within a few seconds.

settings.notLoggedInDesc: Run `calabi login` in a terminal, then refresh this page.
settings.serviceHint: Register the daemon as a system service to auto-start on boot:
settings.serviceNote: Note: install / uninstall requires administrator privileges on Windows / Linux.
settings.configHint: Export all tunnels of the current account as JSON to migrate to another machine or back up.
settings.logoutHint: Signing out calls identity-svc to revoke the current session and clears this machine's access / refresh tokens. The device fingerprint + API key are kept, so no re-pairing is needed next time.
settings.dragHint: Click or drag a .json file here
settings.formatHint: The file must be in calabi-config.json format (schema_version=1)
settings.dryRunDone: Dry-run: {{total}} new tunnel(s) would be created

serviceMode.agentTooltip: This client runs under a fixed identity ({{identity}}); the local console is read-only. Manage tunnels and your account from the web console.
serviceMode.agentManageTooltip: This client runs under a fixed identity ({{identity}}). You can manage this organization's tunnels here; sign-in and org switching are done from the web console.
serviceMode.tunnelsReadonly: Read-only in agent mode — manage tunnels from the web console
serviceMode.agentBannerDesc: This client runs as a service under a pinned API-key identity. Create, edit, and delete tunnels from the web console.
serviceMode.agentManageBannerDesc: This client runs as a service under a pinned API-key identity with the tunnel.write scope. You can manage this organization's tunnels here, just like the web console. Sign-in and org switching stay disabled.

login.title: Sign in to Calabi
login.subtitle: Local client console
login.totpPrompt: Two-factor authentication is on for this account — enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app below.
login.totpInvalid: That verification code didn't match. Check your authenticator app and try again.
login.registerPre: Don't have an account? Register via the

tools.title: Tools / Diagnostics
tools.scanInfo: Lists this machine's listening ports and the address each is bound to
tools.scanInfoDesc: Reads this machine's own listening-socket table locally — nothing leaves the machine, and it never goes to the coordinator. Where the platform can't be enumerated it falls back to a TCP handshake against 127.0.0.1 + ::1 on the common dev ports (extend with CALABI_PROBE_PORTS=3001,4500).
tools.noPortsFound: No listening ports found — your dev server may not be running yet
tools.meshLoopbackOnlyTip: This port only listens on 127.0.0.1, so no other mesh device can reach it. Bind it to 0.0.0.0 or to this machine's overlay address.
tools.meshNotProbedTip: This machine isn't on the mesh right now, so reachability couldn't be checked.

mesh.title: Mesh
mesh.stopConfirm: Stop mesh on this machine? It leaves the meshnet until you start it again.
mesh.pausedDesc: Mesh is stopped on this machine.
mesh.pausedHint: This device left the meshnet. Click Start to rejoin.
mesh.notConfigured: Mesh is not configured on this daemon.
mesh.notConfiguredHint: Add a mesh: block (coord / relay / auth_key) to the daemon config, then restart.
mesh.unavailable: Mesh status is unavailable on this daemon.

adv.title: Routing (subnet router / exit node)
adv.routesHelp: CIDRs on this machine's LAN to expose to the mesh, e.g. 192.168.1.0/24. Peers reach them through this device.
adv.exitNode: Offer this device as an exit node
adv.exitNodeHelp: Other devices can route their internet traffic out through this machine.
adv.useExit: Route my traffic through an exit node
adv.useExitHelp: This machine's default traffic goes through the named exit peer (its name or overlay IP). Leave empty for none.
adv.saved: Saved — the mesh session restarts to apply it.
adv.noForward: Forwarding only works on Linux. This machine will advertise these, but won't actually forward traffic until it runs on a Linux device.
adv.acceptHelp: Off by default. An accepted route enters this machine's routing table — if it covers a host that also connects to services on this machine, the replies go into the mesh and those connections stall.
adv.excludesHelp: Accept the rest, except these. Excluding a range also refuses the more specific prefixes inside it.

mesh.orgSwitching: This device is still on {{org}}'s mesh; it is re-enrolling into the organization you just switched to.

svc.introDesc: This is a declaration only — an admin confirms it in the web console before any svc: access rule matches it. A port bound to 127.0.0.1 cannot be reached from the mesh; bind it to 0.0.0.0 before declaring.
svc.declared: Declared — waiting for an admin to confirm
svc.publishedTip: Already published as the public tunnel «{{name}}». Manage it on the Tunnels page.
svc.fromConfigTip: This entry comes from --mesh-service or the config file. Change it there; removing it here would be re-declared at the next restart.
svc.reachOkTip: Devices on the mesh can reach this service.
svc.reachLoopbackTip: The service only listens on 127.0.0.1, so other mesh devices can't reach it. Bind it to 0.0.0.0.
svc.reachRemoteTip: The service points at {{target}}, which isn't on this device; the mesh doesn't forward there. Move it onto this device (listen on 0.0.0.0), or enable subnet routing for this device.
svc.reachDownTip: The device can't even reach the service's local address, so the app is probably not running.
svc.reachUnknownTip: No result yet — usually within a minute. UDP services aren't probed.
svc.targetTip: What this machine dials when it checks itself, and the local address used if this service is published as a tunnel. Mesh traffic does NOT pass through it — a peer’s packet arrives on this machine’s mesh address.
svc.fromConsoleTip: A manager registered this one in the web console. This machine still self-checks it, but editing and removing it belong there — adding another one here under the same name would just leave two records, only one of them authorized.
svc.nameInvalid: Use a-z, 0-9 and - only — no spaces, and not starting or ending with -
